findings.location: translation.html — paragraph with Tupperware and bread sentence (Part 1 — "Acepta tus límites")
findings.source_quote: That means if you are an avid bread maker, it’s all right to toss a few loaves of bread into your shopping cart.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a more neutral, widely understood term for "loaves of bread" in Spanish. Replace "unas cuantas barras de pan" with "unas cuantas hogazas/unas cuantas piezas de pan" or simply "unos panes" to match the neutral sense of "loaves."
findings.translation_quote: Eso significa que si eres una panadera entusiasta, está bien poner unas cuantas barras de pan en tu carrito de compras.

findings.location: translation.html — paragraph about fun-loving homemakers (Part 1 — "Imperfect women make good homemakers")
findings.source_quote: Fun-loving, happy, homemakers might have a few dust bunnies under the furniture, but they radiate an aura that draws people to their hearts and homes.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a more natural Spanish expression for "dust bunnies." Replace "algunos pelitos de polvo" with "algunas pelusas de polvo" or "unos peluches de polvo" ("pelusas de polvo" is most idiomatic).
findings.translation_quote: Las amas de casa alegres y divertidas pueden tener algunos pelitos de polvo bajo los muebles, pero irradian un aura que atrae a la gente a sus corazones y hogares.

findings.location: translation.section and translation.html — section heading and possible heading phrasing
findings.suggested_fix: Consider the more idiomatic Spanish rendering "De hermana a hermana" instead of the literal "HERMANA A HERMANA." Either is understandable, but the suggested form reads more naturally as a column title.
